title: Lunch service: 20 meals
narration: Our baseline schedules finish in four and eight hours. For Stage Two, we asked a different production question: can shared batches deliver complete meals without wasting their components?

title: Two orders sharing a side batch
narration: Each order is for ten people. The first main is already cooking. We choose a new main for Order B and one twenty-portion side batch shared across both orders. The plan assigns preparation, cooking, packing and cleaning to actual equipment and workers. Separate cookers allow overlap, while one packing line links each portion to its departure.

title: What happens without the side batch
narration: Here we manually skip the shared side. The mains can still finish, but neither customer receives a complete meal. Twenty component portions become waste. This intervention explains the service objective. It is independently checked, and it is not another optimizer run.

title: Batch selection and scheduling constraints
narration: A program specifies quantity, allocations, equipment, workers and phase times for one batch. It is not a pre-solved whole-kitchen schedule. Programs sharing a unit demand anchor form a one-hot block, including idle. Cross-block conflicts forbid double delivery and shared-resource overlaps. The complete small cell keeps all thirty-two legal programs and three idle choices.

title: Complete meals and food waste
narration: Main coverage times side coverage tells us whether a meal is complete. Their sum minus twice their product counts unpaired components. These expressions expand directly into quadratic program-selection terms, without product qubits. We prioritize missed meals, then waste, then new batches and plan changes. Integer bounds prove that priority order. A separate full-objective bound makes every global ground state feasible.

title: Mandatory cleaning after repair
narration: In the larger disruption case, the repaired cooker cannot resume immediately. Its qualified worker first finishes committed work, then cleans the repaired cooker. The clean occupies both worker and equipment. Freshness, calendars and departures are checked from raw operation records, independently of the QUBO conflict graph.

title: Local QAOA sampling
narration: We now run the local quantum simulator with retained angles. This generates fresh samples without retraining or contacting a quantum device. Every returned bitstring passes through the independent checker. The output shows the objective tuple, complete meals, waste and valid shots. The visible kitchen replay has its own retained source label.

title: Results against exact and classical references
narration: All six small-cell QAOA trials found its optimum, and the simple controls found it too. On the larger pilot, six of eight final incumbents match their final offered-pool optimum. All eight still trail the full-grid reference. Final-step controls also tie. This separates the cost of restricted choices from search quality, without claiming a quantum advantage.

title: VeloxQ at 512–2,048 variables
narration: VeloxQ receives larger instances of this same paired-meal formulation, at five hundred twelve through two thousand forty-eight variables. Our integration preserves integer coefficients, checks the spin convention and validates raw returned schedules. The first cold jobs identify a feasibility bottleneck. This section will feature the owner's final checked settings and comparisons when those results are frozen.

title: Results and implementation
narration: The selected schedule serves twenty meals with no discarded portions. The repository includes the formulation, correctness proofs, source code, checked results and development log.
